"Create a complete, playable 2D top-down survival action roguelike game inspired by Vampire Survivors.

The game should feature the following systems:

1. Player Character

- The player controls a hero using WASD or arrow keys.
- Smooth 360-degree movement.
- The character attacks nearby enemies automatically.
- The player has health, movement speed, attack power, and defense stats.

2. Enemy System

- Enemies continuously spawn from all directions.
- Enemies automatically chase the player.
- Different enemy types with unique movement speeds, health, and abilities.
- Enemy waves become increasingly difficult over time.
- Powerful boss enemies appear every 5 minutes.

3. Weapons and Combat

- Automatically attack enemies with equipped weapons.
- Include swords, magic projectiles, fireballs, lightning, spinning blades, and area-of-effect attacks.
- Weapons can be upgraded to increase damage, attack speed, projectile count, and attack range.
- Add satisfying hit effects, damage numbers, and enemy death animations.

4. Leveling and Upgrades

- Defeated enemies drop experience gems.
- Collect experience gems to level up.
- When leveling up, pause the game and display three random upgrade choices.
- Players can choose new weapons, upgrade existing weapons, or improve character stats.
- Include rare and powerful weapon evolutions.

5. Survival Gameplay

- The objective is to survive for 30 minutes.
- Display a survival timer, health bar, experience bar, level, and kill counter.
- Increase enemy spawn rates and difficulty as time passes.
- Add collectible health items and temporary power-ups.

6. Graphics and Visual Style

- Beautiful 2D pixel-art graphics.
- Dark fantasy atmosphere with forests, graveyards, ruins, and mysterious environments.
- Smooth character animations.
- Colorful magical attacks and impressive visual effects.
- A polished and modern game interface.

7. Game Features

- Main menu with Start Game, Settings, and Restart options.
- Game Over and Victory screens.
- Multiple playable characters with unique abilities.
- Randomized upgrades for high replayability.
- Sound effects and background music.
- Smooth performance even with hundreds of enemies on screen.

8. Important Requirements

- Make the game fully playable, not just a visual demonstration.
- Implement real enemy AI, collision detection, damage calculations, and progression systems.
- Make the gameplay addictive, challenging, and satisfying.
- Use original characters, enemies, weapons, and visual assets.
- Create a complete working game with responsive controls and minimal bugs.

Start by building a playable prototype with player movement, automatic attacks, enemy spawning, experience collection, and level-up upgrades. Then expand it into a polished survival roguelike game. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()
import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

Empty project. Build a static HTML/JS/CSS game (no framework needed; simple static index.html). Could use Vite but static is fine and faster. Must support mobile/tablet touch controls. Need polished pixel art — original assets. Best approach: procedural pixel art rendered via canvas at low internal resolution (e.g., 480x270 or 640x360) scaled up with imageSmoothingEnabled false. Generate sprites procedurally into offscreen canvases at startup with pixel art patterns. That gives real pixel-art look without external assets.

Big task. Let me plan architecture carefully and implement robustly.

Files:
- index.html
- style.css
- src/main.js (or game.js single big file, modular maybe)
- Maybe split: engine.js, sprites.js, data.js, game.js. Since static HTML no bundler, use ES modules via <script type="module">. Works served over HTTP.

Game design:

Canvas internal resolution: 480x270? For a top-down game with hundreds of enemies, 480x270 scaled to 1280 wide (2.67x) gives chunky pixels. Mobile portrait: internal maybe 320x568? Responsive canvas aspect. Simpler: fixed logical playfield resolution based on viewport aspect, e.g., internal height 270, width = 270*aspect. But camera/UI? Better: game world rendered with camera, HUD DOM overlay responsive. Canvas fills viewport; internal render resolution = floor(cssWidth / scale) where scale = 3 desktop, 3 mobile? We can set internal canvas resolution to ~480x270 for landscape desktop; on portrait mobile 390x844 -> internal 195x422 which is odd. Maybe render at 2x device pixels but draw pixel art with nearest scaling and use CSS image-rendering: pixelated. Simpler: fixed internal resolution with letterbox? But requirement phone/tablet support and "usable touch controls" — fullscreen game with touch joystick. We can make canvas render at CSS size * dpr capped, but pixel art drawn at scale 3: use ctx transform scale(3) and draw logical coordinates. Camera in logical world units. Set renderScale = clamp(round(min(vw,vh)/270?), 2..4). Hmm.

Approach: choose a "world view" of fixed logical height (e.g., 260 px) and width = 260 * aspect. Canvas backing store = view logical * pixelScale where pixelScale is integer 3? Actually to look pixelated, draw sprites at integer scale 3 then upscale. We can set canvas width = ceil(logicalW*3), height = ceil(logicalH*3), CSS width 100%. Then ctx.setTransform(3,0,0,3,0,0) and everything in logical units. On phone portrait, logicalW = 260 * (390/844) = 120 — too narrow. Instead fix logical width at ~360 and height = 360/aspect => 779 for portrait, too tall. Better: use a design where world view adapts: logicalW = 480, logicalH = 480/aspect clamped? For portrait 480x1039, huge vertical view. That's actually okay for top-down but zoomed out weird. Alternative: clamp viewport to a max area: choose zoom so the visible world area is ~480x270 landscape but for portrait use 270 wide x 480 tall (rotate the aspect). #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the saved project and publish readiness only after both HTTP checks pass.
set -euo pipefail
cd "${PROJECT_DIR:?}"
: "${OPENCODE_WEB_DIR:?}" "${APP_URL:?}"
PORT="${APP_PORT:-3000}"
export PORT
startup_timeout="${STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:-600}"
[[ "$startup_timeout" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo 'STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS must be a positive integer.' >&2; exit 1; }
/usr/bin/time -p test -f start.sh
/usr/bin/time -p bash -n start.sh
current_commit="${CHECKPOINT_COMMIT:-}"
previous_commit=""
[[ ! -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit" ]] || previous_commit="$(/usr/bin/time -p cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit")"
# Reuse an in-flight build for this checkpoint when a readiness retry returns.
starting=false
if [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit" ]] && [[ "$(/usr/bin/time -p cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit")" == "$current_commit" ]] && /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null; then
  starting=true
fi
if [[ "${RESTART_APP:-false}" == true ]] || { [[ "$starting" == false ]] && { [[ -n "$current_commit" && "$previous_commit" != "$current_commit" ]] || ! /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" >/dev/null; }; }; then
  /usr/bin/time -p rm -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/ready-preview-url"
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux kill-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || true
  /usr/bin/time -p node "${RUNTIME_DIR:?}/scripts/reclaim-preview-port.mjs"
  /usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$current_commit" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit"
  # Pass paths through tmux's environment; keep the script in the foreground.
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux new-session -d -s app-server -c "$PROJECT_DIR" \
    -e "RUNTIME_DIR=${RUNTIME_DIR:?}" -e "OPENCODE_WEB_DIR=$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR" -e "PORT=$PORT" -e "STARTUP_LOG=$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/app.log" \
    'bash start.sh > "$STARTUP_LOG" 2>&1'
fi
ready=false
for ((attempt=0; attempt<(startup_timeout + 1) / 2; attempt++)); do
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || { echo 'Startup process exited. Inspect app.log.' >&2; exit 1; }
  if /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" >/dev/null; then
    ready=true
    break
  fi
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || { echo 'Startup process exited. Inspect app.log.' >&2; exit 1; }
  /usr/bin/time -p sleep 2
done
[[ "$ready" == true ]] || { echo "Local startup failed after ${startup_timeout}s. Inspect app.log." >&2; exit 75; }
/usr/bin/time -p rm -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit"
# Local readiness is independent of a temporary public tunnel failure.
/usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$current_commit" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit"
for ((attempt=0; attempt<12; attempt++)); do
  status="$(/usr/bin/time -p curl --silent --show-error --location --max-time 10 --output "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/public-readiness.log" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$APP_URL")" || status=000
  if [[ "$status" == 2* ]]; then
    /usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$APP_URL" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/ready-preview-url"
    if [[ -n "${OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT:-}" ]]; then
      /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 5 "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT/omgithub/heartbeat" >/dev/null || true
    fi
    echo 'Local and public preview are ready.'
    exit 0
  fi
  if [[ "$status" == 4* && "$status" != 408 && "$status" != 429 ]]; then
    echo "Public preview rejected the request (HTTP $status). Inspect public-readiness.log." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  /usr/bin/time -p sleep 2
done
echo 'Public preview did not become ready.' >&2
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Preview startup needs tmux even when optional SSH access is disabled.
if ! command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  case "${RUNNER_OS:?}" in
    macOS) /usr/bin/time -p brew install tmux ;;
    Linux)
      /usr/bin/time -p sudo apt-get update
      /usr/bin/time -p sudo apt-get install -y tmux
      ;;
    *) echo "Unsupported preview runner: $RUNNER_OS" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
fi
/usr/bin/time -p tmux -V

}

/* ============================================================
   GRAVEWAKE — procedural pixel art
   All sprites, icons and textures are original and generated
   at runtime. No external assets.
   ============================================================ */

export function makeCanvas(w, h) {
  const c = document.createElement('canvas');
  c.width = Math.max(1, w | 0);
  c.height = Math.max(1, h | 0);
  return c;
}

export function ctxOf(canvas) {
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
  return ctx;
}

export function drawMap(map, palette, scale = 1, pad = 0) {
  const w = map[0].length, h = map.length;
  const c = makeCanvas(w * scale + pad * 2, h * scale + pad * 2);
  const g = ctxOf(c);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
    const row = map[y];
    for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
      const ch = row[x];
      const col = palette[ch];
      if (!col) continue;
      g.fillStyle = col;
      g.fillRect(pad + x * scale, pad + y * scale, scale, scale);
    }
  }
  return c;
}

"Create a complete, playable 2D top-down survival action roguelike game inspired by Vampire Survivors.

The game should feature the following systems:

1. Player Character

- The player controls a hero using WASD or arrow keys.
- Smooth 360-degree movement.
- The character attacks nearby enemies automatically.
- The player has health, movement speed, attack power, and defense stats.

2. Enemy System

- Enemies continuously spawn from all directions.
- Enemies automatically chase the player.
- Different enemy types with unique movement speeds, health, and abilities.
- Enemy waves become increasingly difficult over time.
- Powerful boss enemies appear every 5 minutes.

3. Weapons and Combat

- Automatically attack enemies with equipped weapons.
- Include swords, magic projectiles, fireballs, lightning, spinning blades, and area-of-effect attacks.
- Weapons can be upgraded to increase damage, attack speed, projectile count, and attack range.
- Add satisfying hit effects, damage numbers, and enemy death animations.

4. Leveling and Upgrades

- Defeated enemies drop experience gems.
- Collect experience gems to level up.
- When leveling up, pause the game and display three random upgrade choices.
- Players can choose new weapons, upgrade existing weapons, or improve character stats.
- Include rare and powerful weapon evolutions.

5. Survival Gameplay

- The objective is to survive for 30 minutes.
- Display a survival timer, health bar, experience bar, level, and kill counter.
- Increase enemy spawn rates and difficulty as time passes.
- Add collectible health items and temporary power-ups.

6. Graphics and Visual Style

- Beautiful 2D pixel-art graphics.
- Dark fantasy atmosphere with forests, graveyards, ruins, and mysterious environments.
- Smooth character animations.
- Colorful magical attacks and impressive visual effects.
- A polished and modern game interface.

7. Game Features

- Main menu with Start Game, Settings, and Restart options.
- Game Over and Victory screens.
- Multiple playable characters with unique abilities.

7: export function makeCanvas(w, h) {
8:   const c = document.createElement('canvas');
9:   c.width = Math.max(1, w | 0);
10:   c.height = Math.max(1, h | 0);
11:   return c;
12: }

14: export function ctxOf(canvas) {
15:   const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
16:   ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
17:   return ctx;
18: }

20: export function drawMap(map, palette, scale = 1, pad = 0) {
21:   const w = map[0].length, h = map.length;
22:   const c = makeCanvas(w * scale + pad * 2, h * scale + pad * 2);
23:   const g = ctxOf(c);
24:   for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
25:     const row = map[y];
26:     for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
27:       const ch = row[x];
28:       const col = palette[ch];
29:       if (!col) continue;
30:       g.fillStyle = col;
31:       g.fillRect(pad + x * scale, pad + y * scale, scale, scale);
32:     }
33:   }
34:   return c;
35: }

519: function pixelLine(g, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, w = 2) {
520:   g.strokeStyle = color; g.lineWidth = w; g.lineCap = 'square';
521:   g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(x0, y0); g.lineTo(x1, y1); g.stroke();
522: }

524: function glow(g, x, y, r, color) {
525:   const grd = g.createRadialGradient(x, y, 0, x, y, r);
526:   grd.addColorStop(0, color); grd.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(0,0,0,0)');
527:   g.fillStyle = grd; g.fillRect(x - r, y - r, r * 2, r * 2);
528: }

712: export function drawSprite(g, key, x, y, scale = 1, flip = false, alpha = 1) {
713:   const s = SPRITES[key];
714:   if (!s) return;
715:   const w = s.width * scale, h = s.height * scale;
716:   g.save();

732: }

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D top-down survival action roguelike for phone and tablet, inspired by Vampire Survivors.
- Start with a playable prototype, then expand it into a polished game.

## Requirements
- Implement responsive WASD/arrow and touch controls, smooth movement, automatic attacks, chasing enemies, collision and damage.
- Include XP gems, level-up upgrade choices, escalating waves, varied enemies and weapons, bosses every five minutes, stats, pickups, and a 30-minute victory goal.
- Include menus, settings, restart, multiple characters, game-over and victory screens, sound, original pixel-art visuals, and smooth performance.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Build a self-contained static web app without dependencies.
- Generate original visual assets and audio procedurally in code rather than using external assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the app structure in `index.html` and interface styling in `styles.css`.
- Added procedural sprites in `src/sprites.js`, synthesized audio in `src/audio.js`, chunked terrain in `src/world.js`, and game data in `src/data.js`.
- Syntax checks passed for `src/sprites.js`, `src/world.js`, and `src/audio.js`.

### Active
- Finish the game engine and integrate gameplay, UI, and existing modules.
- Test the playable game in a browser and save/check the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html`, `styles.css`, and existing modules to identify DOM IDs and APIs.
2. Implement the game loop, controls, combat, enemy AI/spawning, XP and upgrades, timer, bosses, and win/loss states.
3. Wire menus, settings, HUD, restart, mobile controls, pause/level-up choices, and audio.
4. Run and test the game in-browser; fix issues and save/check the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: application markup and UI screens.
- `styles.css`: game and menu styling.
- `src/sprites.js`: procedural sprite and icon generation.
- `src/audio.js`: generated music and sound effects.
- `src/world.js`: procedural biome terrain and chunk rendering.
- `src/data.js`: characters, weapons, passives, enemies, bosses, pickups, waves, and stat formulas.

## Important Context
- Gameplay implementation, UI wiring, browser testing, and screenshot checks are not yet recorded as completed.
- Prior oversized write calls intermittently timed out upstream; splitting writes into smaller chunks worked afterward.
- No commit or push state was reported.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D top-down survival action roguelike for phones and tablets, inspired by Vampire Survivors.
- Start with a playable prototype, then expand it into a polished game.

## Requirements
- Implement responsive keyboard and touch controls, smooth movement, automatic attacks, chasing enemies, collision and damage.
- Include XP gems, level-up upgrades, escalating waves, varied enemies and weapons, five-minute bosses, stats, pickups, and a 30-minute victory goal.
- Include menus, settings, restart, multiple characters, game-over and victory screens, sound, original pixel-art visuals, and smooth performance.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Build a self-contained static web app without dependencies.
- Generate original visual assets and audio procedurally in code rather than using external assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created app structure and interface styling in `index.html` and `styles.css`.
- Added procedural sprites in `src/sprites.js`, synthesized audio in `src/audio.js`, chunked terrain in `src/world.js`, and game data in `src/data.js`.
- Syntax checks passed for `src/sprites.js`, `src/world.js`, and `src/audio.js`.

### Active
- Finish the game engine and integrate gameplay, UI, and existing modules.
- Test the playable game in a browser and save/check the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining markup and module APIs to identify DOM IDs and integration points.
2. Implement the game loop, controls, combat, enemy AI/spawning, XP and upgrades, timer, bosses, and win/loss states.
3. Wire menus, settings, HUD, restart, mobile controls, pause/level-up choices, and audio.
4. Run and test the game in-browser; fix issues and save/check the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: application markup and UI screens.
- `styles.css`: game and menu styling.
- `src/sprites.js`: procedural sprite and icon generation.
- `src/audio.js`: generated music and sound effects.
- `src/world.js`: procedural biome terrain and chunk rendering.
- `src/data.js`: characters, weapons, passives, enemies, bosses, pickups, waves, and stat formulas.

## Important Context
- Gameplay implementation, UI wiring, browser testing, and screenshot checks are not yet recorded as completed.
- Prior oversized write calls intermittently timed out upstream; splitting writes into smaller chunks worked afterward.
- No commit or push state was reported.

186:     ? (player.stats.multishot || 0) : 0;
187:   const dmg = d.damage * (1 + 0.26 * (lvl - 1)) * (evo ? 1.75 : 1) * (1 + (player.stats.might || 0) * 0.12);

189:   const area = (1 + 0.07 * (lvl - 1)) * (evo ? 1.3 : 1) * (1 + (player.stats.area || 0) * 0.10) * (player.charArea || 1);

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D top-down survival action roguelike for phones and tablets, inspired by Vampire Survivors.
- Start with a playable prototype, then expand it into a polished game.

## Requirements
- Implement responsive keyboard and touch controls, smooth movement, automatic attacks, chasing enemies, collision and damage.
- Include XP gems, level-up upgrades, escalating waves, varied enemies and weapons, five-minute bosses, stats, pickups, and a 30-minute victory goal.
- Include menus, settings, restart, multiple characters, game-over and victory screens, sound, original pixel-art visuals, and smooth performance.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Build a self-contained static web app without dependencies.
- Generate original visual assets and audio procedurally in code rather than using external assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created app structure and interface styling in `index.html` and `styles.css`.
- Added procedural sprites in `src/sprites.js`, synthesized audio in `src/audio.js`, chunked terrain in `src/world.js`, and game data in `src/data.js`.
- Syntax checks passed for `src/sprites.js`, `src/world.js`, and `src/audio.js`.
- Inspected UI markup, game data, world APIs, sprite APIs, audio APIs, and styles to identify integration points.

### Active
- Implement the game engine and integrate gameplay, UI, and existing modules.
- Test the playable game in a browser and save/check the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `src/main.js` and wire the existing markup, data, world, sprites, and audio modules.
2. Implement the game loop, controls, combat, enemy AI/spawning, XP and upgrades, timer, bosses, and win/loss states.
3. Wire menus, settings, HUD, restart, mobile controls, pause/level-up choices, and audio.
4. Run and test the game in-browser; fix issues and save/check the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: application markup and UI screens; loads `src/main.js`.
- `styles.css`: game and menu styling.
- `src/data.js`: characters, weapons, passives, enemies, bosses, pickups, waves, and stat formulas.
- `src/sprites.js`: procedural sprites, icons, portraits, and drawing helpers.
- `src/world.js`: procedural biome terrain and chunk rendering.
- `src/audio.js`: generated music and sound effects.

## Important Context
- Gameplay implementation, UI wiring, browser testing, and screenshot checks are not yet completed.
- The referenced `src/main.js` does not yet appear in the repository file listing.
- Prior oversized write calls intermittently timed out upstream; splitting writes into smaller chunks worked afterward.
- No commit or push state was reported.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D top-down survival action roguelike for phones and tablets, inspired by Vampire Survivors.
- Start with a playable prototype and expand it into a polished game.

## Requirements
- Implement responsive keyboard and touch controls, smooth movement, automatic attacks, chasing enemies, collision and damage.
- Include XP gems, level-up upgrades, escalating waves, varied enemies and weapons, five-minute bosses, stats, pickups, and a 30-minute victory goal.
- Include menus, settings, restart, multiple characters, game-over and victory screens, sound, original pixel-art visuals, and smooth performance.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Build a self-contained static web app without dependencies.
- Generate original visual assets and audio procedurally in code rather than using external assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created app structure and interface styling in `index.html` and `styles.css`.
- Added procedural sprites in `src/sprites.js`, synthesized audio in `src/audio.js`, chunked terrain in `src/world.js`, and game data in `src/data.js`.
- Added the initial `src/main.js` implementation for UI setup, character selection, run state, level-up choices, stats, and screen transitions.

### Active
- Finish the game engine and integrate gameplay, controls, combat, enemy AI/spawning, XP and upgrades, bosses, pickups, and HUD updates.
- Test the playable game in a browser and save/check the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` with movement, drawing, combat, enemy behavior and spawning, XP collection, bosses, pickups, and the frame loop.
2. Wire menu/settings/how-to/pause/restart/quit/end-screen controls, keyboard input, and touch joystick.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests; fix issues and save/inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: active gameplay and UI integration; currently incomplete.
- `index.html`: UI markup and module entry point.
- `styles.css`: game and menu styling.
- `src/data.js`: character, weapon, passive, enemy, boss, pickup, wave, and stat definitions.
- `src/world.js`: procedural terrain and biome APIs.
- `src/sprites.js`: procedural sprites, icons, portraits, and drawing helpers.
- `src/audio.js`: generated music and sound effects.

## Important Context
- `src/main.js` was just created and currently ends after `updateHud()`; the game loop and gameplay systems are not yet implemented.
- No browser testing, screenshot checks, or commit/push state has been reported.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, polished, playable 2D top-down survival roguelike for phones and tablets, inspired by Vampire Survivors.

## Requirements
- Include responsive keyboard and touch movement, automatic attacks, chasing enemies, collision and damage, XP and upgrades, escalating waves, varied weapons and enemies, bosses every five minutes, pickups, and a 30-minute victory goal.
- Include menus, settings, restart, multiple characters, game-over and victory screens, sound, original pixel-art visuals, and smooth performance.
- Avoid clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Build a self-contained static web app without dependencies.
- Generate original visual assets and audio procedurally in code.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created UI markup and styling, procedural sprites, synthesized audio, chunked terrain, game data, and initial menu/run/level-up/HUD setup.

### Active
- Finish gameplay systems and wire controls, menus, settings, pause, restart, and end screens.
- Test the playable game in a browser and save/inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after `updateHud()` with movement, drawing, combat, enemy AI/spawning, XP collection, bosses, pickups, and the frame loop.
2. Wire keyboard and touch controls plus menu, settings, how-to, pause, restart, quit, and end-screen actions.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests; fix issues and save/inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Current integration work; ends after `updateHud()`, with gameplay loop and event wiring still missing.
- `index.html`: Game HUD and screen markup, with IDs used by `main.js`.
- `styles.css`: Responsive game and UI styling.
- `src/data.js`: Character, weapon, passive, enemy, boss, pickup, wave, and stat definitions.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural terrain and biome APIs.
- `src/sprites.js`: Procedural sprites, icons, portraits, and drawing helpers.
- `src/audio.js`: Generated music and sound effects.

## Important Context
- `src/main.js` already imports game data, `World`, sprite helpers, and `AudioEngine`; it creates the initial UI setup, run state, level-up choice logic, passive effects, and HUD updates.
- No gameplay loop, browser testing, screenshot checks, or commit/push state has been reported.

178: export function weaponStat(w, player) {
179:   const d = WEAPONS[w.id];
180:   const lvl = w.level;
181:   const evo = w.evolved ? 1 : 0;
182:   const amountBase = d.amount || 0;
183:   const amountFromLevel = d.type === 'projectile' || d.type === 'pierce' || d.type === 'explosive' || d.type === 'lightning' || d.type === 'orbit' || d.type === 'zone'
184:     ? Math.floor((lvl - 1) / 3) : 0;
185:   const multishot = (d.type === 'projectile' || d.type === 'pierce' || d.type === 'explosive' || d.type === 'lightning' || d.type === 'orbit' || d.type === 'zone')
186:     ? (player.stats.multishot || 0) : 0;
187:   const dmg = d.damage * (1 + 0.26 * (lvl - 1)) * (evo ? 1.75 : 1) * (1 + (player.stats.might || 0) * 0.12);
188:   const cd = d.cooldown * Math.pow(0.93, lvl - 1) * (evo ? 0.72 : 1) * Math.pow(0.92, player.stats.haste || 0) * (player.charCooldown || 1);
189:   const area = (1 + 0.07 * (lvl - 1)) * (evo ? 1.3 : 1) * (1 + (player.stats.area || 0) * 0.10) * (player.charArea || 1);
190:   const amount = Math.max(1, amountBase + amountFromLevel + multishot + (evo ? 2 : 0));
191:   const pierce = (d.pierce || 0) + (evo ? 99 : Math.floor((lvl - 1) / 4));
192:   return {
193:     damage: dmg, cooldown: cd, area, amount, pierce,
194:     range: (d.range || 0) * area, radius: (d.radius || 0) * area,
195:     speed: d.speed || 0, arc: (d.arc || 0) * (0.9 + area * 0.1),
196:     duration: (d.duration || 0) * area,
197:   };
198: }

200: export function weaponUpgradeText(w) {
201:   const d = WEAPONS[w.id];
202:   const next = w.level + 1;
203:   const parts = [];
204:   parts.push('+26% damage');
205:   if (next % 2 === 0) parts.push('faster cast');
206:   if (next % 3 === 1 && next > 1) parts.push('+1 projectile');
207:   if (next >= 5) parts.push('wider area');
208:   return parts.slice(0, 2).join(' · ');
209: }

## Objective
- Build a polished, playable 2D top-down survival roguelike for phones and tablets, inspired by Vampire Survivors.

## Requirements
- Include responsive keyboard and touch movement, automatic attacks, chasing enemies, collision and damage, XP and upgrades, escalating waves, varied weapons and enemies, bosses every five minutes, pickups, and a 30-minute victory goal.
- Include menus, settings, restart, multiple characters, game-over and victory screens, sound, original pixel-art visuals, and smooth performance.
- Avoid clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Build a self-contained static web app without dependencies.
- Generate original visual assets and audio procedurally in code.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created UI markup and styling, procedural sprites and audio, terrain, game data, and initial menu, run, level-up, and HUD setup.

### Active
- Finish gameplay systems and wire controls, menus, settings, pause, restart, and end screens.
- Test the playable game in a browser and save/inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after `updateHud()` with movement, drawing, combat, enemy AI/spawning, XP collection, bosses, pickups, and the frame loop.
2. Wire keyboard and touch controls plus menu, settings, how-to, pause, restart, quit, and end-screen actions.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests; fix issues and save/inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Integration work; currently ends after `updateHud()`, with gameplay loop and event wiring still missing.
- `index.html`: Game screens, HUD, controls, and IDs used by `main.js`.
- `styles.css`: Responsive game and UI styling.
- `src/data.js`: Character, weapon, passive, enemy, boss, pickup, wave, and stat definitions.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural terrain and biome APIs.
- `src/sprites.js`: Procedural sprites, icons, portraits, and drawing helpers.
- `src/audio.js`: Generated music and sound effects.

## Important Context
- `src/main.js` imports data, `World`, sprite helpers, and `AudioEngine`; it creates initial UI setup, run state, level-up choice logic, passive effects, and HUD updates.
- The latest attempted edit failed with `newString: Missing key`; no change from that attempt was applied.
- No gameplay loop, browser testing, screenshot checks, or commit/push state has been reported.

178: export function weaponStat(w, player) {
179:   const d = WEAPONS[w.id];
180:   const lvl = w.level;
181:   const evo = w.evolved ? 1 : 0;
182:   const amountBase = d.amount || 0;
183:   const amountFromLevel = d.type === 'projectile' || d.type === 'pierce' || d.type === 'explosive' || d.type === 'lightning' || d.type === 'orbit' || d.type === 'zone'
184:     ? Math.floor((lvl - 1) / 3) : 0;
185:   const multishot = (d.type === 'projectile' || d.type === 'pierce' || d.type === 'explosive' || d.type === 'lightning' || d.type === 'orbit' || d.type === 'zone')
186:     ? (player.stats.multishot || 0) : 0;
187:   const dmg = d.damage * (1 + 0.26 * (lvl - 1)) * (evo ? 1.75 : 1) * (1 + (player.stats.might || 0) * 0.12);
188:   const cd = d.cooldown * Math.pow(0.93, lvl - 1) * (evo ? 0.72 : 1) * Math.pow(0.92, player.stats.haste || 0) * (player.charCooldown || 1);
189:   const area = (1 + 0.07 * (lvl - 1)) * (evo ? 1.3 : 1) * (1 + (player.stats.area || 0) * 0.10) * (player.charArea || 1);
190:   const amount = Math.max(1, amountBase + amountFromLevel + multishot + (evo ? 2 : 0));
191:   const pierce = (d.pierce || 0) + (evo ? 99 : Math.floor((lvl - 1) / 4));
192:   return {
193:     damage: dmg, cooldown: cd, area, amount, pierce,
194:     range: (d.range || 0) * area, radius: (d.radius || 0) * area,
195:     speed: d.speed || 0, arc: (d.arc || 0) * (0.9 + area * 0.1),
196:     duration: (d.duration || 0) * area,
197:   };
198: }
199: 
200: export function weaponUpgradeText(w) {
201:   const d = WEAPONS[w.id];
202:   const next = w.level + 1;
203:   const parts = [];
204:   parts.push('+26% damage');
205:   if (next % 2 === 0) parts.push('faster cast');
206:   if (next % 3 === 1 && next > 1) parts.push('+1 projectile');
207:   if (next >= 5) parts.push('wider area');
208:   return parts.slice(0, 2).join(' · ');
209: }

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a polished, playable 2D top-down survival roguelike for phones and tablets, inspired by Vampire Survivors.

## Requirements
- Include responsive controls, automatic combat, enemies, upgrades, escalating waves, bosses, pickups, a 30-minute victory goal, menus/settings, multiple characters, sound, and original pixel-art visuals.
- Avoid clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained static web app without dependencies; generate original visual assets and audio procedurally.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, procedural visuals/audio, terrain, data, menus, gameplay systems, controls, combat, upgrades, pickups, bosses, settings, pause, restart, and end screens.
- Fixed the `BIOMES` import in `src/main.js`; syntax checks passed for `src/main.js`, `src/world.js`, and `src/data.js`.
- Updated button styling and removed menu-panel, brand, brand-mark, and button-glint animations while investigating unreliable automated clicks.
- Captures completed with auto-start disabled earlier; the latest strict capture reported desktop auto-start failure and mobile auto-start success.

### Active
- Validate gameplay start and interactions on desktop and mobile.
- Complete strict auto-start capture, then save and inspect the latest small JPEG.

### Blocked
- Desktop automated start click remains intermittent. The latest strict run logged `Capture desktop: auto-start not-actionable`; a direct reproduction also timed out during `performing click action` after reporting the button visible, enabled, and stable. Removing several animations has not resolved it.

## Next Move
1. Investigate why automated desktop clicks on `#startBtn` time out, then rerun strict capture.
2. Validate gameplay controls and interactions on desktop and mobile.
3. Save a small JPEG and inspect only the latest image.
4. Report assumptions and validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Gameplay systems, UI wiring, controls, rendering, and `#startBtn` handler.
- `src/data.js`: Character, weapon, passive, enemy, boss, pickup, wave, and stat definitions.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural terrain and `BIOMES` export.
- `index.html`: Game screens and controls, including `#startBtn`.
- `styles.css`: Responsive UI and recent animation/button changes.
- `capture.sh`: Browser screenshot/validation entry point.
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/capture-start.mjs`: Auto-start logic; trial and actual click use 2-second timeouts.
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-capture.mjs`: Strict desktop/mobile capture flow.
- `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/wip-screenshots.cjs`: Screenshot output handling.
- `/tmp/opencode/repro-capture.mjs`: Direct reproduction of the intermittent desktop click failure.

## Important Context
- App responds at `http://localhost:3000/`.
- Strict capture command: `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3000 CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/opencode/gravewake-capture CAPTURE_STRICT=1 ./capture.sh`.
- Latest strict capture reached mobile with auto-start clicked, but desktop reported not-actionable.
- Repository files remain untracked; no commit or push was reported.
